claim: SWE-bench evaluates whether language models can resolve real-world GitHub issues by generating a patch that passes the repository's tests; it is an issue-resolution (bug-fix) benchmark, not a review-comment-quality benchmark.
quote: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-world Github Issues?

claim: On the SWE-bench Verified leaderboard in 2026, top frontier models report resolution rates around 82-88%, with leading entries such as GPT-5.5 (~82.6%) and Claude Opus 4.7/4.8 (~82-88%).
quote: GPT 5.5 leads with a performance of 82.60%, with Claude Opus 4.7 following closely at 82.00%

claim: SWE-bench Multimodal contains 619 task instances from 17 user-facing JavaScript repositories (web UI, data visualization, mapping), testing whether coding agents generalize to visual software domains.
quote: SWE-bench Multimodal ... 619 task instances ... 17 ... JavaScript ... repositories

claim: Systems perform far worse on SWE-bench Multimodal than on text-only SWE-bench, with top resolve rates historically in the low double digits (~12%), reflecting a large penalty when visual inputs are involved.
quote: the top resolve rate reaching only 12.2%

claim: The CodeReviewer dataset (Microsoft, EMNLP/FSE 2022) is a large multilingual corpus across nine languages used to benchmark three code-review tasks: code change quality estimation, review comment generation, and code refinement.
quote: Automating Code Review Activities by Large-Scale Pre-training

claim: The CodeReviewer dataset comprises roughly 150,406 training, 13,103 validation and 13,104 test examples drawn from top-starred GitHub repositories across nine popular languages.
quote: CodeReviewer ... real-world code changes and code reviews from open-source projects in nine of the most popular programming languages

claim: CRScore (NAACL 2025) is a reference-free metric grounding evaluation of code-review comments in LLM/static-analyzer-detected claims and code smells, scoring conciseness, comprehensiveness and relevance.
quote: CRScore: Grounding Automated Evaluation of Code Review Comments in Code Claims and Smells

claim: CRScore achieves the best alignment with human judgment among open-source metrics (0.54 Spearman) and ships a corpus of ~2.9k human-annotated review-quality scores for machine-generated and GitHub review comments.
quote: greatest alignment with human judgment among open source metrics (0.54 Spearman correlation) ... corpus of 2.9k human-annotated review quality scores

claim: CodeReviewQA (MSR 2025) is a comprehension benchmark of 900 manually curated instances across 9 languages that decomposes code refinement into three reasoning stages: Change Type Recognition, Change Localisation, and Solution Identification, to expose model weaknesses and reduce contamination.
quote: Change Type Recognition (CTR) ... Change Localisation (CL) ... Solution Identification (SI) ... 900 manually curated, high-quality examples ... 9 languages

claim: Martian's open-source Code Review Bench evaluates AI code-review agents using both an offline benchmark (identical PRs with known issues) and an online benchmark that measures whether developers accept or reject AI review comments in real repositories.
quote: Code Review Bench - Code Review Benchmark | Martian

claim: Martian's Code Review Bench is derived from over 200,000 pull requests (drawing on 1.2M+ real code changes from GitHub PRs involving AI bots), is updated daily, and open-sources the dataset, judge prompts, and pipeline; Martian sells no coding assistant, claiming independence.
quote: largest benchmark ... derived from more than 200,000 pull requests and updated daily ... Over 1.2 million real code changes

claim: Qodo claims #1 on Martian's benchmark with its Extended (Research Preview) config at F1 64.3% (precision 62.3%, recall 66.4%), while its Standard production version scores F1 47.9% (#4).
quote: F1 Score: 64.3% Precision: 62.3% Recall: 66.4% ... Qodo Standard ... F1 Score: 47.9% ... #4

claim: CodeRabbit separately claims #1 on Martian's online benchmark over ~300,000 PRs (Jan-Feb 2026) with F1 51.2%, precision 49.2%, recall 53.5%, illustrating that vendors cite different configs/time windows for their top-ranked claims.
quote: highest F1 score 51.2% ... Precision 49.2% ... Recall 53.5% ... nearly 300,000 pull requests

claim: RepoBench (ICLR 2024) benchmarks repository-level code auto-completion in Python and Java via three tasks (RepoBench-R retrieval, RepoBench-C completion, RepoBench-P pipeline), each with up to ~12,000 evaluation samples across multiple context-length levels.
quote: RepoBench: Benchmarking Repository-Level Code Auto-Completion Systems
